Choose the sentence with the same meaning as the following.
I exercise alone every weekday.
I went home right after finishing the meeting.
I stopped by home before the meeting.
This shop does not sell fruit.
I went straight home after the meeting ended.
Choose the sentence with the same meaning.
A weekday exercise habit differs in both topic and action from the event of returning home after a meeting.
“전에” (before) refers to the time before the meeting, reversing the order in the original “끝난 후에” (after it ended). “들렀습니다” (stopped by) also differs from going straight home.
Whether a shop sells fruit has nothing to do with returning home after a meeting.

【Answer evidence】The original “회의가 끝난 후에 바로 집에 갔습니다” (I went straight home after the meeting ended) means returning home immediately after the meeting. “회의를 마치고 곧 집으로 갔습니다” (I went home right after finishing the meeting) has the same event order and action. The correct expression is “회의를 마치고 곧 집으로 갔습니다.” (I went home right after finishing the meeting.)
【Distractor trap】The key trap is reversing “후에(뒤에)” (after) into “전에(앞에)” (before). The exercise and fruit-selling options are unrelated to the meeting and returning home.
【How to solve this type】For same-meaning questions, briefly mark the subject, action, and time order. In this sentence, keep only the option preserving both parts of ‘회의 종료 → 즉시 귀가’ (meeting ends → immediate return home).
In the current option order, choice 2 is correct.

Since last year, I have been stretching for ten minutes when I get up in the morning. At first, it was difficult because my body was stiff, but after about a month, moving became easier. Above all, the short duration made it less burdensome, so I could keep doing it. That is why I think it is important to start a new habit small enough to do every day rather than starting big from the outset.

The outside of the building looks the same as before, but inside are photographs of the area and belongings of local residents. When traveling, people tend to think it is important to see many famous places. But I like trips where I stay in one city for a long time. When I visit the same market for several days, I begin to notice things I did not see on the first day. I exchange greetings with shopkeepers and learn the neighborhood’s daily rhythms. That is when the destination starts to look not merely like a sight to see, but like someone’s everyday life.
